newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Solana asks E. Europe to treat Russia with respect.
newsitem.headline: Solana asks E. Europe to treat Russia with respect.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana said on Thursday that eastern European countries eager to join the alliance had to commit themselves to maintaining good ties with Russia.

"The opening of NATO in no sense, in no way, aims to isolate or marginalise Russia," he told leading politicians and business executives -- including Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin -- at the annual World Economic Forum in Davos.
"That is why we would expect those countries wishing to join the alliance to be as committed to a good, constructive relationship with Russia as member countries are," he said.

NATO is keen to have a security accord with Russia ready for July when a summit in Madrid will name the alliance's first new members for over two decades. Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic lead the field with Romania and Slovenia close behind.
"I am convinced that we we will achieve increased security in Europe in cooperation with Russia," Solana said at the gathering of political and business leaders.
